question.prompt:
Points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D\) are on a circle of diameter \(1,\) and \(X\) is on diameter \(\overline{AD}.\) If \(BX=CX\) and \(3\angle BAC=\angle BXC=36^\circ,\) then \(AX=\)

[Figure 1](figures/1993_AMC_12_Q23_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The condition \(BX=CX\) suggests finding the perpendicular bisector of \(BC\), because that line will reveal the relevant angle bisectors.

Let \(O\) be the circle's center. We have \(\angle BAC=12^\circ\), so the inscribed angle theorem gives a minor central angle \(\angle BOC=24^\circ\). Hence \(X\ne O\), since \(\angle BXC=36^\circ\). Both \(O\) and \(X\) are equidistant from \(B\) and \(C\), so the line through them is the perpendicular bisector of \(BC\). Because both lie on the diameter \(AD\), this line is \(AD\).

In particular, \(AB=AC\). The perpendicular bisector of the base of isosceles triangle \(ABC\) bisects its vertex angle, so
\[
\angle BAX=\frac12\angle BAC=6^\circ.
\]
Here \(X\ne A\), since otherwise \(\angle BXC\) would equal \(12^\circ\).

We must choose the correct angle at \(X\). In isosceles triangle \(BXC\), the perpendicular bisector of \(BC\) bisects the \(36^\circ\) vertex angle. Thus the ray \(XA\) either makes \(18^\circ\) with \(XB\), or makes its supplement \(162^\circ\).

Since \(AD\) is a diameter, \(\angle ABD=90^\circ\). Also, \(X\) lies on the segment \(AD\), so \(\angle ABX\le90^\circ\). If \(\angle BXA=18^\circ\), the angle sum in triangle \(ABX\) would give \(\angle ABX=156^\circ\), which is impossible. Therefore
\[
\angle BXA=162^\circ,
\qquad \angle ABX=12^\circ.
\]
In right triangle \(ABD\), the hypotenuse is \(AD=1\) and \(\angle BAD=6^\circ\), giving \(AB=\cos6^\circ\). Now the sine rule in triangle \(ABX\) gives
\[
\frac{AX}{\sin12^\circ}
=\frac{AB}{\sin162^\circ}
=\frac{\cos6^\circ}{\sin18^\circ}.
\]
Since \(\sin18^\circ>0\), this division is valid. Using \(\csc18^\circ=1/\sin18^\circ\), we obtain
\[
\boxed{AX=\cos6^\circ\sin12^\circ\csc18^\circ},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Use symmetry to solve triangle ABX
